comparisons.peer_summary: Commitments accounted for under the fair value option had a notional amount of $2.2 billion and $2.6 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023, with cumulative net fair values of $144 million and $67 million classified in accrued expenses and other liabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose the notional amount and fair value of commitments accounted for under the fair value option. JPM reported lending-related commitments of $12.2 billion with a fair value of $50 million as of December 31, 2024. BAC reported commitments of $2.2 billion with cumulative net fair values of $144 million for the same date. JPM's elected commitment amount was significantly larger than BAC's, and JPM reported a net liability (negative fair value relative to principal implied by the context of lending commitments typically being liabilities or off-balance sheet exposures with fair value adjustments), whereas BAC explicitly reports a positive cumulative net fair value classified in accrued expenses.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting treatment of loans at fair value
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value within Trading assets, with changes recognized in earnings. This accounting treatment excludes these loans from the allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and MS discuss the accounting treatment for items (loans and commitments) for which the fair value option is elected. JPM discloses specific elected lending-related commitments ($12.2 billion) and their fair values. MS discloses the general policy that loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value with changes recognized in earnings, and notes that allowance for credit losses do not apply to these loans and lending commitments. While JPM provides the quantitative balance of elected commitments, MS provides the qualitative accounting framework excluding these items from credit loss models.

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024 and 2023, the contractual amount of lending-related commitments for which the fair value option was elected was $12.2 billion and $9.7 billion, respectively, with a corresponding fair value of $50 million and $97 million, respectively.
Loans for which the fair value option is elected are carried at fair value and included in Trading assets in the balance sheet, with changes in fair value recognized in earnings.
Because such loans and lending commitments are reported at fair value, the allowance for credit losses and charge-off policies do not apply to these loans.
